QF.id: AIFM CIII Modern Portfolio Theory and Capital Market Theory_8

question.text: Mr. Vivek Joshi, CIO of Chambal Managed Futures Fund, explains the Efficient Frontier to a new analyst. Which statement BEST describes the efficient frontier?

answer.text: The set of portfolios with the highest possible Sharpe ratio for any given correlation.
The set of portfolios offering the maximum expected return for each given level of risk (or minimum risk for a given return).
A straight line connecting the risk-free asset to the market portfolio.
The locus of portfolios with zero systematic risk.

explanation.text: The Logic: Workbook page 55 defines the efficient frontier as the set of portfolios providing the maximum rate of return for a given level of risk (or minimum risk for a given rate of return). It is the upper envelope of the feasible set of risky-asset combinations. The Trap: (A) mixes CML with the efficient frontier — Sharpe maximisation applies to a single tangent portfolio, not the full frontier. (C) describes the CML, not the efficient frontier. (D) is unrelated; zero systematic risk is not how the frontier is defined. Note: In practice, Cat III funds operate inside a constrained frontier shaped by source-backed limits — the 2x leverage cap (pages 63 and 409) and the investee-concentration caps (page 77). The textbook frontier definition still anchors the answer.
